findings.summary: admitStaleRenegotiation defaults runSlug to prdSlug, which is the kiro-only run-state filename, while the same call derives provider-qualified branch and worktree names — a caller that omits runSlug for any other provider reads and writes the wrong run-state file.
findings.evidence: src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:621 `const runSlug = args.runSlug ?? args.prdSlug;` feeds loadRunState/transactRunState, whose statePath is `.afk/state/<slug>.json` (src/run-state.ts:594-596). Real runs key that file by run slug: src/orchestrator.ts:738 `return runSlugForProviderName(prdSlug, provider.name);` and :2188-2191 `const runSlug = pipelineRunSlug(...); loadRunState(repoRoot, runSlug)`, i.e. `<prdSlug>-claude-code` for every non-kiro provider (src/run-identity.ts:23-28). The same call already provider-qualifies the branch (`featureBranchForProviderName`) and worktree (`sliceWorktreeDirForProviderName`) at src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:383-392. The fixture cements the mismatch rather than exposing it: src/preserve-work-recovery.test.ts:61 uses PROVIDER = "claude-code" yet writes state at `${PRD_SLUG}.json` (:206), so every green admission test runs the pairing a real launch never produces.
findings.expected: One admission call resolves every run-scoped identity through src/run-identity.ts, so the run-state file it locks is the same file the run's own writers lock (B-08's ADR 0056 recheck and B-09's append are both against that file).
findings.observed: The default run-state slug is provider-unqualified. With provider "claude-code" and no explicit runSlug, admission would load an absent `.afk/state/<prdSlug>.json`, refuse with `scope-absent`, or — if such a file existed — append the PENDING event beside the real run's state instead of into it. No shipped entry point can reach this today, because parsePipelineRuntimeOptions refuses every well-formed request until #335 (B-12), so the defect is latent.
findings.clearCondition: With a non-kiro provider name and no explicit runSlug argument, admission reads and appends to the same run-state file the run's own writers use (the run-identity-derived slug), and a test exercises that provider-qualified pairing rather than a fixture whose provider and state filename disagree.

findings.summary: Worktree registration is inferred from the presence of a `.git` file in the expected directory, so a survivor directory git no longer tracks reads as registered and admission proceeds.
findings.evidence: src/preserve-work-recovery.ts:397 `if (!existsSync(worktreeDir) || !existsSync(join(worktreeDir, ".git")))` is the whole `worktree-unregistered` check, and the comment at :393-396 explains registration is read off the filesystem to keep eligibility's git surface at the three predicates P-05 pins. The fixture supplies exactly that shape by hand — src/preserve-work-recovery.test.ts:167-169 writes a `.git` file containing `gitdir: ...` into a plain directory and every eligible case passes — so no test distinguishes a real linked worktree from a leftover directory. This repo already treats worktree survivors as a live condition (`formatWorktreeSurvivorWarning`, src/git.ts:469-472).
findings.expected: B-05: the target "has a recorded slice branch and a registered worktree at it" — registration being what git records, per the contract's phrasing.
findings.observed: Any directory containing a `.git` entry at the derived path satisfies the check, including a worktree whose removal failed and which git no longer lists; admission can then record a PENDING attempt against a worktree git does not track.
findings.clearCondition: A directory that carries a `.git` entry but is not a worktree git tracks is refused with `worktree-unregistered`, and a test covers that case alongside the missing-directory case.
